title: The Weirdest Thing to Me About the Machine: Satisfaction For Nothing
author: AsparagusOk8818
selftext:
...So, I don't know if anyone else has this experience and feels strange about it:  

  
I get a lot of anti-AI stuff in my feeds. I can't help myself - I'm as much a slave to these fckn algorithms as anyone else - so I watch them. Honestly, there's a lot of good stuff in there even if I disagree with a lot of the fundamentals. People are very right to be skeptical of how much wealth and power is being concentrated right now, IMHO.

But anyway, one of the things that is constantly brought up is how the machine will rob us of the sense of satisfaction at doing a job. Since it is doing the job, well, that should make me feel like a bystander and no longer happy about a thing being done. 

In abstract, I agree. This is how things seem like they should work. The machine is doing the heavy lifting for the coding, I should not feel the satisfaction of the code work being done since I am not doing it. 

But... experientially, that's not what happens. I totally feel the satisfaction of the work being done, just as if I had been the one doing it. I get the full dopamine hit. 

I guess my brain just doesn't actually give a shit if I did the work or not; it only cares that the work was done and I was somehow involved. 

  
This is weird to me and kind of disquieting. It's usually kind of dangerous, addiction-wise, to have access to a very easy source of dopamine. And addiction is one of those things that sneaks up on you and just starts controlling your life while you don't really notice. 

  
...Anyone else experiencing this and think it is weird? Anyone else maybe just a teeny bit concerned about the easy access to dopamine the machine is providing?

comments.author: Haster
comments.body:
I don't find it's that weird. It's no different than if I used a tool to do anything else. Could I have moved the bolder without the tractor? in time surely but the results are what matter; the boulder is gone and I'm happy about that.

I remember people saying the same thing about the satisfaction of having found the information myself in the library. They might not have been entirely wrong, I don't get the same satisfaction from using google, but I get to move on to the fucking point of what I'm trying to accomplish and the results are what I want in the end.

comments.author: CrimsonBolt33
comments.body:
You have to remember, a lot of anti AI people are talking from the point of it being a moral and emotional issue ("AI is bad/wrong, has no feelings, robs us of dignity" etc, nonsense that means nothing)...not from a technical or experienced perspective.

I don't know why people are so quick to attribute so many emotional, philosophical, moral, and human like things to AI.

It's a tool....have you never found a tool or thing in your life that improved it a lot before?

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
I don't know what world those people live in. Work is work. I don't feel "satisfaction" for doing a job. I feel satisfaction with enjoying the finished product.

I patched and painted my entire basement last year and updated all the lighting fixtures and switches. It gave me zero satisfaction. In fact, it was annoying, physically demanding, and required a lot of prep and cleanup work.

I like the way it looks now that it's done, but I don't like it *more* because I did the work myself. I'd get the same satisfaction if I hired someone to do it.

And these are also people that actively don't use AI. I'll admit I used to be somewhat like that. Shit changed quick once I started using it at work and seeing what it's capable of. And it's still work. The work gets done faster, but it's still a bunch of work and effort to make something good.

comments.author: FidoTheDogFacedBoy
comments.body:
> how the machine will rob us of the sense of satisfaction at doing a job

There’s more satisfaction than ever, because I can do things I used to dream of doing. But there’s more frustration than ever, because the computer balks in the weirdest ways beyond anything you could ever imagine.
